items.title: Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom lead chip stocks lower as AI trade comes under pressure
items.summary: Chip giant Nvidia led semiconductor stocks lower on Tuesday.

items.title: Stocks give back gains as Anthropic dips below IPO price
items.summary:
Hosts Julie Hyman and Jake Conley, joined on the couch by Barron's markets reporter Jacob Sonenshine, tackle the top stories of the day. Including futures sliding after Monday's biggest rally since April 2025, Anthropic briefly trading below its $83 IPO price, a Wall Street Journal report that the U.S. is preparing new tariffs on China and dozens of other countries, and whether Jensen Huang's return leaves Nvidia owing a favor to the White House.

The team is joined by Seaport Research Partners senior analyst Jay Goldberg and Creative Strategies CEO and principal analyst Ben Bajarin to discuss what Jensen Huang needs to tell shareholders, the competitive threat from Broadcom and AMD, and whether Nvidia's financing of neoclouds is a wobbly foundation. The show closes on Strategy trading below the value of its Bitcoin, Sanofi's $41 billion deal for Insmed, and a strong day for retail earnings from Best Buy, Dollar Tree, Dick's, Abercrombie, and Kohl's.

items.title: Novanta Shares Just Jumped And We’re Buying This Robotics Play
items.summary: Just as early investors targeted foundational chipmakers like Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM), Nvidia (NVDA), and Broadcom (AVGO) at the start of the AI computing wave, investors are currently examining diversified industrial and sensor plays such as Regal Rexnord (RRX), Timken (TKR), Allegro MicroSystems (ALGM), Ouster (OUST), and STMicroelectronics (STM). During a recent episode of The AI Investor Podcast, hosts Eric Bleeker and Austin Smith took a closer look at Novanta, and shared why they are optimistic about the robotics manufacturer as an AI investment play to target in 2027.
